title: plan_shares: a large Vietnamese plan returns HTTP 500 — the route trims the snapshot by CHARACTER count (MAX_SNAPSHOT_JSON=60000) but the DB CHECK limits BYTES (pg_column_size(plan) <= 65536), and Vietnamese is multi-byte
repro_steps: POST /api/plans/share (authenticated) with a full 10-day x 12-item itinerary of diacritic-heavy Vietnamese text. toPlanShareSnapshot trims to <=60000 CHARS (planShare.ts:55,121-127 use JSON.stringify(s).length), but the trimmed snapshot's UTF-8 size stays > 65536 BYTES, so the plan_shares_plan_check CHECK rejects the insert.
evidence: Live on audit project: a snapshot measured 76908 chars / 135844 bytes; /api/plans/share -> 500 {error:server_error} (the DB CHECK pg_column_size(plan)<=65536 failed; plan_shares_plan_check). planShare.ts MAX_SNAPSHOT_JSON=60000 counts chars; the migration 20260913_plan_shares.sql CHECK counts bytes. src/app/api/plans/share/route.test.ts MOCKS the insert (returns {data:{id}} unconditionally), so the suite is GREEN over this.
impact: Sharing a large itinerary (the app is Vietnamese-first, so byte inflation is systematic) fails with an opaque 500 instead of succeeding or a graceful message. No data loss, no security issue.
root_cause: An app-level bound (60000 chars) that does not match the DB constraint it exists to satisfy (65536 bytes), compounded by multi-byte UTF-8; and a mocked-insert test that never exercises the real byte CHECK.
fix: fitBudget() in planShare.ts now measures Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(s),'utf8') against MAX_SNAPSHOT_BYTES=56000 (renamed from the 60000-char MAX_SNAPSHOT_JSON), ~9.5 KiB below the 65536-byte CHECK.
verification: Live: the exact 135,844-byte Vietnamese plan that 500-ed in PASS 3 now returns 200 and persists. Confirmed the CHECK is on pg_column_size which is the TOAST-COMPRESSED datum size: a repetitive payload stored at 1283 bytes (10 days trimmed to 5); a VARIED (poorly-compressible) Vietnamese payload stored 47,522 text bytes at pg_column_size 12,785 (all 10 days kept) — far under 65536. So the 56000 raw-text-byte budget guarantees pg_column_size stays well under the CHECK in every realistic case. Unit test added with realistic Vietnamese content asserting byteLength <= budget and budget < 65536; 31/31 plan-share tests pass; tsc 0.
notes: Schema-wide audit for the CLASS: plan_shares.plan is the ONLY byte-based DB constraint (pg_column_size); no octet_length/::bytea CHECK exists on any other public table, so no other route has this char-vs-byte mismatch. (F-030 remains the broader test-suite-blind-spot finding.)

title: fn_grant_admin_role trusts p_actor_id as a PARAMETER (not auth.uid()) and its only defense is the service_role-only EXECUTE grant — currently SAFE (authenticated cannot call it), but fragile
repro_steps: Live on the audit project: sign in as an ordinary user (manual.uat.fresh@tappyai.com) with the ANON key to obtain that user's own authenticated JWT (is_anonymous=false, role=authenticated); with that JWT (NO service-role key) call rpc('fn_grant_admin_role', { p_actor_id: <some OTHER user's uid>, p_user_id: <a target uid>, p_role: 'admin' }).
evidence: Result: HTTP error 42501 'permission denied for function fn_grant_admin_role'; data null; and a service-role read of admin_roles for the target returns 0 rows — no grant occurred. Contrast: the same RPC called with the SERVICE-ROLE key succeeds (used during UAT account provisioning). So EXECUTE is service_role-only. Source: 20260803_platform_owner.sql:201 `GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION fn_grant_admin_role(...) TO service_role;` — there is NO matching `REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM PUBLIC/authenticated`; the deny relies on PUBLIC not holding the default function EXECUTE in this project. The function body (20260803_platform_owner.sql:84-118) takes p_actor_id as a parameter, checks only p_actor_id<>p_user_id (self-promotion) and, for super_admin, fn_is_platform_owner(p_actor_id); it never reads auth.uid() and never verifies the CALLER is an admin/owner.
impact: No exploit today: an ordinary authenticated (or anonymous) user cannot execute the function, so the two-account admin self-grant is blocked at the grant layer. The risk is latent/fragile: because the actor is a trusted parameter and the caller is never authorization-checked, the function's ONLY safeguard is the EXECUTE grant. If that grant were ever widened to `authenticated`/`anon`/PUBLIC (a stray GRANT, a schema-reset that restores PUBLIC's default function EXECUTE, or a future migration), any user could self-grant `admin` (and, if they could also pass the platform-owner uid, potentially super_admin) with two accounts — instant P0 privilege escalation.
root_cause: Defense-in-depth of one layer: the SECURITY DEFINER function authorizes by a caller-supplied p_actor_id rather than auth.uid()+a role check, so it is only as safe as its EXECUTE grant, which is asserted positively (GRANT TO service_role) but not reinforced by an explicit REVOKE FROM PUBLIC/authenticated.
fix: Migration 20260921_f032_admin_role_actor_from_authuid.sql (+ rollback): fn_grant_admin_role and fn_revoke_admin_role now derive the actor from the VERIFIED request instead of trusting p_actor_id. Service-role callers (the app's createAdminClient — the /api/admin/rbac/roles route authorizes the admin via requirePermission FIRST, then calls through the service-role client) are allowed and keep p_actor_id only as the audit granted_by; detected by auth.jwt()->>'role'='service_role' (a claim no client can forge — PostgREST sets it from the verified JWT). Any other caller must prove via auth.uid() they are the platform owner or an active super_admin/admin, else 42501; p_actor_id is ignored for the authz decision so spoofing it gains nothing. Same treatment for fn_revoke_admin_role. No signature change (ACL preserved, no caller breaks). §3 re-asserts REVOKE EXECUTE FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated on both (all three grantees, because Supabase's ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES grants new functions to anon+authenticated explicitly — a bare REVOKE FROM PUBLIC is insufficient, which is exactly what holds the line today per 20260807_platform_owner_revoke_public_execute.sql).
verification: DB test supabase/tests/admin_role_actor_boundary.test.ts (18 cases, embedded-postgres): grant layer (anon/authenticated -> 42501 'permission denied for function'; has_function_privilege shows service_role only) AND body layer via impersonated request.jwt.claims (service_role grants, granted_by=p_actor_id; admin-own-JWT grants, granted_by=auth.uid() with p_actor_id IGNORED; plain user 42501 even when spoofing p_actor_id=owner, 0 rows; unauthenticated 42501; self-promotion blocked; super_admin owner-only; fn_revoke likewise), plus idempotency, a source assertion that the forward migration never GRANTs to anon/authenticated, and a rollback check (restores the trust-the-caller body while keeping the lockdown). APPLIED to the audit project (direct DB, ref-guarded) — idempotent; ACL after = service_role (+owner) only, body references auth.jwt()/auth.uid(). LIVE over PostgREST: (1) plain-user JWT spoofing p_actor_id=admin -> 42501, no admin_roles row; (2) service-role grant succeeds (granted_by=the admin uid); (3) admin via own JWT -> 42501 (grant layer). The 3 requested release verifications all pass.
notes: The three-verification set requested by the owner all pass. Requirement 3 answer (what revokes the default PUBLIC EXECUTE today): 20260807_platform_owner_revoke_public_execute.sql explicitly REVOKEs EXECUTE on these functions FROM PUBLIC, anon AND authenticated — necessary because on Supabase two independent grants reach a new function (Postgres' PUBLIC default AND ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public GRANT ALL ON FUNCTIONS TO anon, authenticated, service_role), so PUBLIC-only revokes leave anon/authenticated able to call it. The app route /api/admin/rbac/roles is unaffected (uses the service-role client after its own requirePermission gate; granted_by unchanged = the acting admin's id). Distinguishing service_role from an ordinary caller: the request JWT role claim (service_role carries role='service_role' and no auth.uid(); an end user carries role='authenticated' with their sub).

verification: Trace confirmed by code read (commerce.ts / feedHints.ts / feedIngest.ts / cron/feed-ingest/route.ts / vercel.json). Resolver machinery works when given a product hint (adapters/resolver tests green); the absence is data, not a broken resolver.
notes: Owner-flagged. Track to launch: a shipped app with no buy buttons is a revenue outage even though no code is wrong. | ACCESSTRADE creds: ACCESSTRADE_API_KEY + ACCESSTRADE_FEED_ENDPOINT are ABSENT from .env.local (also PUBLISHER_ID, CJ_API_KEY, CRON_SECRET) — feed-ingest cron cannot run; prod launches with zero buy buttons until Accesstrade approval. LAUNCH FALLBACK ASSESSMENT (analysis only, owner decides): (a) the FREE Serper /shopping `link` is a google.com/search?prds= REDIRECT (measured 40/40, OfferRow.tsx:25-29) — a search shape both offerDestination/linkDepth and CCP ownedUrl reject, exactly what A3.3 bans; it already renders today, correctly labelled as a `search` link, NOT a buy button; 0 extra API cost but wrong shape. (b) The only Serper-derived REAL product URLs are the site:shopee/tiki/lazada /search results (shopping.ts:94-104) — and these are ALREADY what CCP discovery (commerce.ts:559) consumes to build depth-3 detail links; when discovery finds an identity-matched product page the system ALREADY renders it DIRECT/untracked without Accesstrade (resolve.ts:86-88 keeps build.url when wrapper disabled/unavailable) and affiliate_click ALREADY fires tracked=false (commerceTap: tracked = c.tracked===true). So the owner-desired direct+tracked=false behavior EXISTS for discovered links; no new plumbing needed there. The real limiter is COVERAGE: discovery + the empty feed rarely yield an identity-matched product page (productIdentity.ts is strict), so buy-button coverage stays low pre-approval regardless. More pre-approval coverage would require loosening discovery (more Serper /search calls per query = API cost + the wrong-product/dead-link/non-VN risk A3.3 + productIdentity deliberately guard). Instrumenting the non-CCP /shopping OfferRow anchor would need a new onClick and only a free-text seller name (no provider slug).
